# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** [GAP-1] and the [state of divine order] [GAP-2] surpasses [GAP-3] the proceeding divine truth flowing through those heavenly societies.

**¶3:** This one, whom the heavenly societies acknowledged as "confirmed in good" [GAP-4] — they confirmed him in the midst of the heavenly states of wisdom. These manifold goods and truths in their plenitude distinguished him and set him apart, and he proceeded forth against the principle of falsity from evil. They gave this essential quality [GAP-5] this very subject [GAP-6] who are manifold, who dwell within the heavenly states of wisdom and who [GAP-7: REVIEW are beyond] all limit or enumeration.

**¶4:** This one, [GAP-8: REVIEW whom they acknowledged as] "in perfect alignment with divine order," because he is the first principle of divine order who had no falsity from evil among all the heavenly states that belong to wisdom and to the interior perception [GAP-9] they perceived him inwardly, so that [GAP-10] his inmost Divine, which had sent him forth with five essential powers of the spiritual mind [GAP-11] into spiritual destruction.

**¶5:** This one also [GAP-12: REVIEW whom they acknowledged as] "uniquely proceeding from the Divine," because he was established [GAP-13] to pour forth [GAP-14] the principle of falsity from evil.

**¶7:** Again, just as the uniquely proceeding goods from your [GAP-15: REVIEW uniquely] proceeding celestial lineage, and you [GAP-16] according to the external natural principle [GAP-17] uniquely proceeding also from celestial good and spiritual truth and all the [GAP-18] of the whole of created spiritual reality.

**¶8:** Just as your inmost Divine, the Primordial Divine Human, himself maintained his integrity in the [GAP-19: REVIEW midst] of all the states of evil and falsity. He had no affection for [GAP-20: REVIEW the] states of evil and falsity, nor any concupiscence toward them! Rather, his interior perception and celestial love directed toward those who belong to him in good and truth remain within him. Whatever else the principle of falsity from evil [GAP-21] through its forcible falsifications — behold, the Divine Human labors and sustains spiritual combat, so that evil may be separated from those who are his own and cast out from among them. And he purifies them and liberates them from bondage, and restores them to their original celestial state as they were from the beginning.

**¶10:** [GAP-22] may they recover the living interior perception of those who belong to him in good and truth, as he abides in this state through all conditions of obscurity and of illumination without ceasing.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [the love] and the [righte]o[usness of the Father] is more than [the greatness of] the voice through them.

This one, whom they called “approved” [this name was given to him because] they approved him in the midst of the ae[ons of] light. These numerous multitudes set him a[part], and he came forth against the Enemy. They gave this name [to him on account of] this matter [of all those] who are numerous, that are in the aeons of light and who [are without] measure or number.

This one, [whom they called] “righteous”, because he is the first righteous one who had no sin amongst all of the aeons that belong to the light and the thought [by which] they knew him, so that [he pleased] his Father, who had sent him with five sons [against] perdition.
This one also [whom they called] “only begotten”, because he was established [alone to] pour [out against the] Enemy.

Again, just as the only begotten ones from your [only] begotten race and you [are begotten] according to flesh [so also is he the o]nly begot-ten also from gold and silver and all the [treasures] of the universe.

Just as your father, [the F]irst Man, himself stood firm in the [midst] of all the worlds of darkness. He did not love [the] worlds of darkness, nor did he lust for them! Rather, h[is] thought and love for the household of his people is in h[i]m. Anything else that the Enemy [did to them] with his violent de[e]ds. Behold, (the First Man) toils and struggles; so that (the Enemy) would be separat[e from] them and be cast out from them. And he purifies them and ma[ke]s them f[r]ee, and makes them as they were from the beginning.
[And so] may they discover the remembrance of the household of his peo[ple], as he remains in this [place ni]ght and day.

fills.explanation: In Swedenborg, divine love pairs with divine order (righteousness) as the two essentials of the Divine; "the love and the righteousness" is a natural Kephalaia doublet surpassing the external voice (proceeding truth).

Completes "righteousness" and attributes it to the Father (the inmost Divine), consistent with the chapter's theme of the Father sending forth the First Man; the righteousness of the Father surpasses the proceeding voice.

The interior love and righteousness surpasses even "the greatness of the voice" (the full magnitude of proceeding divine truth); "greatness" is a standard Kephalaia term for the measure of divine qualities.

fills.explanation: Follows the chapter's etymological pattern where each divine title receives a causal explanation; the medium gap requires more than a bare "because," and this framing phrase ("this name was given to him because") is the standard Kephalaia formula for introducing the first and fullest name-etymology in a series.
Standard Kephalaia construction linking a divine name to its reason: "They gave this name to him on account of this matter" introduces the etymological explanation of the title "approved."
Provides the antecedent for the relative clause "who are numerous, that are in the aeons of light" — the matter concerns all those manifold beings dwelling in the heavenly states of wisdom.
Confirming the editor's choice; "are without measure or number" is the standard Kephalaia formula for describing the innumerable aeons/multitudes of light.
Confirming the editor's choice; "whom they called" follows the identical etymological formula used for each divine title throughout this chapter (¶3 "approved," ¶4 "righteous," ¶5 "only begotten").

Connects "the thought" (interior perception) to "they knew him" — the thought by which the aeons perceived the righteous one inwardly, forming a standard relative construction in Kephalaia teaching discourse.
In the context of the "righteous" etymology, pleasing the Father connects to divine approval and perfect alignment with divine order; the one without sin pleased his Father who sent him forth.
The Father sent the First Man with his five sons against perdition (the realm of spiritual destruction/darkness), reflecting the Manichaean narrative of the Primal Man's martial mission against evil.
Confirming the editor's choice; identical etymological formula as in ¶3 and ¶4, introducing the third divine title "only begotten" with the same construction used throughout the chapter.

Connects to the "only begotten" etymology — he was established alone (uniquely, as the sole one) to pour forth against the Enemy, explaining why he bears the title of unique proceeding from the Divine.

Standard martial language in Manichaean cosmology: the First Man was established to pour himself out against the Enemy (the principle of falsity from evil), describing the combat between light and darkness.
Confirming the editor's choice; "only begotten race" maintains the consistent use of "only begotten" throughout ¶7's comparison between natural and spiritual begetting.

Fits the "only begotten" etymological discussion: "you are begotten according to flesh" establishes the natural-plane parallel to the spiritual begetting from gold and silver (celestial good and spiritual truth).

In the Kephalaia, "treasures" is the standard term for the precious cosmic substances of light distributed throughout creation; gold, silver, and all the treasures correspond to celestial good, spiritual truth, and all divine knowledges.
Confirming the editor's choice; "in the midst of all the worlds of darkness" is the standard Kephalaia description of the First Man maintaining his integrity while surrounded by evil states.
Confirming the editor's choice; "the worlds of darkness" requires the definite article, paralleling the identical phrase in the preceding clause.

Describes what the Enemy inflicted on the light particles through violence; "anything else that the Enemy did to them" is followed by the First Man's labor to separate and purify them from these violent deeds.
Standard Kephalaia concluding formula introducing a final benediction or wish: "And so may they discover the remembrance..." closes the chapter with a prayer for continual interior perception.
